findings.description: The instance user-data embeds an AWS access key ID and secret access key. User data can be retrieved by principals with instance access or metadata/user-data permissions and is commonly retained in Terraform state and deployment records, exposing reusable credentials.

SSH (TCP/22) is allowed from 0.0.0.0/0. The attached instance is placed in a public subnet with a default route to an Internet Gateway and receives a public IP, making administrative access reachable from any Internet host.

The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true or a KMS key. Its contents, and the snapshot created from it, may be stored unencrypted at rest unless account-level default EBS encryption is enabled outside this configuration.
The flow-log archive bucket has no server-side encryption configuration. Sensitive network-flow records written to this bucket are not explicitly protected with SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS at rest.
